Part 1 · Fundamentals

What chemistry and physics decide how far SO₂ can be converted to SO₃ — and how fast?

Part 1 · the plan

Five ideas that every converter number comes from

  1. Three reactions, one catalystwhich step is reversible and why only it needs V₂O₅
  2. The mass balancefrom 40.9 t/h of sulfur to 238.5 kNm³/h of gas and 125 t/h of acid
  3. Equilibrium$K_p$, the equilibrium conversion $X_e$, and the four levers that move it
  4. Rate and strike temperaturewhy the catalyst needs heat and why the best temperature falls as $X$ rises
  5. Heat balance and double absorptionthe adiabatic line, the staircase, and how 96 % becomes 99.8 %

1 · Three reactions, one catalyst

Sulfur to acid in three chemical steps

$$\begin{aligned} &\text{1 Burning (F-101):} && \mathrm{S(l)} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{SO_2} && \Delta H \approx -297\ \text{kJ/mol}\\ &\text{2 Oxidation (R-201):} && \mathrm{SO_2} + \tfrac12\mathrm{O_2} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO_3} && \Delta H = -98.5\ \text{kJ/mol}\\ &\text{3 Absorption (T-301/302):} && \mathrm{SO_3} + \mathrm{H_2O}\,(\text{in acid}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H_2SO_4} && \Delta H \approx -130\ \text{kJ/mol} \end{aligned}$$

Only step 2 is reversible: it stops at an equilibrium and needs a catalyst to run at all.

Steps 1 and 3 go to completion. Everything the converter operator does serves step 2.

2 · The mass balance

From the sulfur rate to the gas flowstep 1 of 3

Step 1 burns every mole of sulfur to one mole of SO₂. So the sulfur rate fixes the SO₂ flow.

$\dot n_S$
sulfur burned (= SO₂ made), from FIC-103
kmol/h
$y_0$
SO₂ mole fraction of the gas (AIC-104 measures it)
–
$\dot V$
gas flow at 0 °C, 1 atm (1 kmol = 22.414 Nm³)
Nm³/h
$$\dot V = \frac{\dot n_S}{y_0}\times 22.414$$

Strength $y_0$ is chosen by the designer; the air flow follows from it.

2 · The mass balance

The design numbers, reproducedstep 2 of 3

From the previous slide$\dot V = \dfrac{\dot n_S}{y_0}\times 22.414$
$\dot n_S = \dfrac{40\,940}{32.06} = 1277\ \text{kmol/h}$sulfur 40.94 t/h, 32.06 kg/kmol
$\dot V_{F\text{-}101} = \dfrac{1277}{0.14}\times 22.414 = 204.4\ \text{kNm}^3/\text{h}$combustion air, furnace gas 14 % SO₂
$\dot V_{R\text{-}201} = \dfrac{1277}{0.12}\times 22.414 = 238.5\ \text{kNm}^3/\text{h}$after dilution air, 12 % SO₂ into bed 1

Dilution air = 238.5 − 204.4 = 34.1 kNm³/h (FIC-102).

2 · The mass balance

Acid made and oxygen left overstep 3 of 3

Stoichiometry of steps 1–3$\dot m_{acid} = \dot n_S\,X\,M_{H_2SO_4}$  ·  $y_{O_2}+y_{SO_2} = 0.21$
$\dot m_{acid} = 1277 \times 0.998 \times 98.08 = 125.0\ \text{t/h}$one H₂SO₄ per SO₂ converted (99.8 %)
$y_{O_2} = 0.21 - y_{SO_2}$S + O₂ → SO₂ keeps the moles of gas constant
$y_{O_2} = 0.21 - 0.12 = 0.09$9 % O₂ into bed 1, O₂/SO₂ = 0.75

Raising the strength always lowers the O₂ left for step 2.

3 · Equilibrium

The equilibrium constant $K_p$

The mass balance gave the feed gas. How much of its SO₂ can react is set by equilibrium.

$y_i$
mole fraction of SO₂, O₂, SO₃ in the gas
–
$P$
absolute pressure (35 kPa g at bed 1 ≈ 1.35 atm)
atm
$T$
gas temperature
K
$K_p$
equilibrium constant of step 2
atm$^{-1/2}$
$$K_p = \frac{y_{SO_3}}{y_{SO_2}\,\sqrt{y_{O_2}P}}\,,\qquad \log_{10}K_p = \frac{4956}{T} - 4.678$$

Correlation used by the OTS model; exothermic, so $K_p$ falls as $T$ rises.

3 · Equilibrium

Writing $K_p$ in terms of conversionstep 1 of 2

$X$
fraction of the SO₂ fed that has become SO₃
–
$y_0,\ o_0$
SO₂ and O₂ mole fractions of the feed (0.12, 0.09)
–
$\mathrm{SO_2}: y_0(1-X)\quad \mathrm{SO_3}: y_0X\quad \mathrm{O_2}: o_0-\tfrac12 y_0X$basis 1 mol feed; ½ O₂ per SO₃
$N = 1-\tfrac12 y_0 X$total moles fall by ½ per SO₃ made
$\dfrac{y_{SO_3}}{y_{SO_2}} = \dfrac{X}{1-X}$same denominator $N$ cancels

3 · Equilibrium

The equilibrium conversion $X_e$step 2 of 2

Definition of $K_p$ · previous slide$K_p = \dfrac{y_{SO_3}}{y_{SO_2}\sqrt{y_{O_2}P}}$  ·  $\dfrac{y_{SO_3}}{y_{SO_2}}=\dfrac{X}{1-X}$  ·  $y_{O_2}=\dfrac{o_0-\frac12 y_0X}{1-\frac12 y_0X}$
$$\frac{X_e}{1-X_e} = K_p\,\sqrt{\frac{P\,\left(o_0-\tfrac12 y_0X_e\right)}{1-\tfrac12 y_0X_e}}$$

$X_e$ is on both sides: solve by trial (bisection). Valid for ideal gas, no side reactions.

At 631 °C, $K_p = 6.4$ and $X_e = 63\ \%$: bed 1 leaves at equilibrium.

Interactive · move temperature and strength

How far can the reaction go?

Equilibrium, from 3$\dfrac{X_e}{1-X_e} = K_p\sqrt{\dfrac{P(o_0-\frac12 y_0X_e)}{1-\frac12 y_0X_e}}$
$K_p$
$X_e$

Above 500 °C every 50 °C costs 8–14 points of $X_e$, and stronger gas costs more — hot and strong gas cannot convert far.

3 · Equilibrium

Four levers that raise $X_e$

Lower temperature

$K_p$ rises as $T$ falls; floor set by the strike temperature.

More O₂ per SO₂

Weaker gas raises $o_0/y_0$ but means more gas.

Higher pressure

1.5 mol become 1. Set by the blower: 1.35 atm.

Remove SO₃

Absorb it between beds (T-301): the strongest lever.

4 · Rate and strike temperature

The rate of oxidation on V₂O₅

Equilibrium says how far. The catalyst decides how fast — and it needs heat.

$r$
SO₂ converted per kg catalyst
kmol·kg⁻¹·s⁻¹
$k$
rate constant: $k_0e^{-E/R\,(1/T-1/T_0)}$, $E$ = 90 kJ/mol
kmol·kg⁻¹·s⁻¹
$f_{strike}$
0 → 1 as $T$ crosses the strike temperature
–
$$r = k\,f_{strike}\,\sqrt{y_{O_2}}\left(y_{SO_2}-\frac{y_{SO_3}}{K_p\sqrt{y_{O_2}P}}\right)$$

The bracket is zero at equilibrium: the driving force, not just $k$, sets the rate.

4 · Rate and strike temperature

The catalyst's temperature window

V₂O₅–K₂SO₄ on silica works as a molten salt film. Below the strike (light-off) temperature the melt freezes and the rate collapses.

Caesium promoter lowers the strike, so beds 4–5 run cooler.

Above ~640 °C the catalyst sinters.

Interactive · move the conversion already reached

The best temperature falls as conversion rises

Rate, from 4$r = k f_{strike}\sqrt{y_{O_2}}\Big(y_{SO_2}-\dfrac{y_{SO_3}}{K_p\sqrt{y_{O_2}P}}\Big)$
fastest at
rate is zero at

Fresh gas reacts fastest hot; nearly converted gas only reacts if cool — so later beds need lower inlet temperatures.

5 · Heat balance

Why the bed temperature rises with conversionstep 1 of 2

The beds have no cooling inside, so the heat of step 2 stays in the gas.

$\dot n$
total gas flow through the bed
kmol/s
$\bar c_p$
mean molar heat capacity of the gas
kJ·kmol⁻¹·K⁻¹
$\lambda$
adiabatic temperature rise per unit conversion
K
$\dot n\,\bar c_p\,dT = (-\Delta H)\,\dot n\,y_0\,dX$heat released = heat taken by gas
$T-T_{in} = \lambda\,(X-X_{in}),\quad \lambda = \dfrac{y_0(-\Delta H)}{\bar c_p}$integrate; $\bar c_p$ and $\dot n$ nearly constant

5 · Heat balance

3.35 °C for every 1 % convertedstep 2 of 2

From the previous slide$T-T_{in} = \lambda\,(X-X_{in})$,   $\lambda = \dfrac{y_0(-\Delta H)}{\bar c_p}$
$\lambda = \dfrac{0.12\times 98\,500}{35.3} = 335\ \text{K}$$\bar c_p$ ≈ 35.3 kJ/kmol·K near 520 °C
$T_{out} = 420 + 335\times 0.631 = 631\ ^\circ\text{C}$bed 1: 420 °C in, 63.1 % out

Matches TI-203 = 631 °C at design; 13 % SO₂ would give 3.6 °C per %.

From conversion to stack ppmstep 2 of 2

What the intermediate absorber buys

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • Sulfur rate fixes SO₂; strength fixes the gas flow; O₂ = 21 % − SO₂.
  • Equilibrium falls with temperature: 12 % gas stops at 63 % near 631 °C.
  • The catalyst only works above its strike temperature, and later beds want it cooler.
  • Each bed rises 3.35 °C per % converted, so the converter is a staircase.
  • Removing SO₃ between passes lifts 95.8 % to 99.8 % and the stack to 292 ppm.

1 · Emission target

The permit sets the conversion

Stack ppm, from Part 1$\text{ppm} = 10^6\,y_0(1-X)/\varphi$
$1-X = \dfrac{500\times10^{-6}\times 0.821}{0.12} = 0.0034$permit 500 ppm, $\varphi$ = 0.821
$X \ge 99.66\ \%$minimum overall conversion

Single absorption stops near 98 %: the permit forces double absorption.

The design margin, 99.80 % against 99.66 %, is what operators spend on upsets.

3 · The 3 + 2 arrangement

Why the IPA sits after bed 3

Pass 1 · beds 1–3

Strong, fast gas. Three stages reach 95.8 %, where the curve flattens.

IPA · T-301

Removes 99.95 % of the SO₃. The remaining 0.6 % SO₂ now faces almost no product.

Pass 2 · beds 4–5

Dilute, cold gas: Cs catalyst lights off lower and finishes at 99.8 %.

4 · Heat integration

Where 140 MW of heat goes

The IPA returns gas at 83 °C. Only beds 1–2 can reheat it to 425 °C, through E-202 then E-201.

So bed 4 inlet depends on how much heat beds 1–2 give up.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • A 500 ppm permit demands 99.66 %: only double absorption gets there.
  • 12 % SO₂ balances blower size against bed 1 temperature and equilibrium.
  • 340 m³ of catalyst in five beds; Cs catalyst in the cool second pass.
  • Each bed has its own best inlet; later beds run cooler.
  • Beds 1–2 reheat the IPA return gas, so bed 4 hangs on pass 1 heat.

1 · A normal shift

Six things to check every round

Stack SO₂

Bed rises

Each bed's ΔT against design: 211 / 83 / 25 / 16 / 0.

1 · A normal shift

Read each bed's conversion from its rise

Adiabatic line, Part 1$T-T_{in}=\lambda\,(X-X_{in})$,   $\lambda$ = 3.35 °C per % at 12 % SO₂
$\Delta X_2 = \dfrac{528-445}{3.35} = 24.8\ \%$bed 2: design 63.1 → 88.1 %
$\lambda_2 = \dfrac{0.0060\times 98\,500}{33} \approx 18\ ^\circ\text{C}$pass 2 gas holds only 0.60 % SO₂
$\dfrac{441-425}{18} \approx 0.9$bed 4 converts ~90 % of what reaches it

A shrinking rise means less reaction; a growing bed 4 rise means extra SO₂ arriving.

The Converter profile display does this sum for you (X calc row).

2 · The operating handles

Four handles and what they move

Sulfur rate · FIC-103

Production. Air follows by ratio.

Strength · AIC-104

Stronger gas: hotter beds, much higher stack.

Bed inlets · TIC-201…241

Move each bed along its curve: the optimising handle.

Acid · T-301/302

Strength and flow decide SO₃ removal and mist.

3 · Optimising the bed inlets

Where the stack SO₂ is decided

Part 1 showed the best temperature falls as conversion rises — but only while the rate keeps up.

  • Bed 1 leaves at equilibrium: keep TI-203 below 640 °C.
  • Beds 2–3: a few degrees cooler lets them approach a higher equilibrium.
  • Bed 4 a little hotter speeds the dilute gas: the stack's biggest lever.

Interactive · inlets limited to their alarm bands

Cut the stack SO₂ at full rate

stack SO₂
bed 1 exit
overall

Cooler beds 2–3 and a hotter bed 4 pass the 230 ppm target — the direction the graded optimisation run rewards.

3 · Optimising the bed inlets

Why the simulator is harder than the slider

The slider sets each inlet freely. In the plant, beds 1–2 supply the bed 4 heat: a hotter bed 1 also warms bed 4.

Cool bed 2 → less heat to E-201 → TV-231 must close to hold bed 4.

Move one set point, let pass 2 settle (~10 min), then the next.

4 · Start-up

The cold start-up in seven moves

Part 1: the catalyst is dead below its strike temperature. So heat comes first, sulfur last.

K-101 air 80–120 kNm³/h→HV-112 open→H-101 fired→TIC-201 AUTO, preheat→bed 1 ≥ 400 · bed 4 ≥ 360 °C→HV-112 locked shut · acid on→sulfur in via SIS, ≤ 25 %

Then H-101 off, loops to AUTO, air on ratio, and the rate raised in steps.

4 · Start-up · reference run on the OTS

4 h 33 min from cold to lined out

0–3.2 h preheat: bed 1 reaches 500 °C, bed 4 creeps to 360 °C.

3.2 h sulfur admitted at 12 t/h.

3.2–4.4 h rate raised in five steps; stack peaks, then settles.

4 · Start-up

The start-up line HV-112: open to heat, locked to run

During preheat the IPA return gas is cold, so E-201/E-202 cannot warm bed 4.

HV-112 sends hot furnace gas straight to bed 4 until TI-232 passes 360 °C.

In operation HV-112 stays locked closed and is checked on every round.

5 · Shutdown

Planned stop: leave the beds hot and clean

sulfur to ≤ 25 t/hstop sulfur on the SISsweep until stack < 50 ppmstop K-101stop acid pumps · all MAN

18 minutes on the reference run.

Interactive · runs of the OTS model after the sulfur stops

Keep the air on, or stop the blower?

bed 1 middle below 400 °C after
bed 4 below 360 °C after

Air sweeping the beds cools them below the restart permissives within the hour — sweep only until the SO₂ is gone, then stop the blower.

5 · Hot restart

From hot standby to full rate in about an hour

Blower first, H-101 at least 30 s later (air ≥ 60 kNm³/h).

Start the acid pumps just before sulfur: they are a permissive.

Sulfur in at 11 min; lined out at 35 min; 58 min graded.

5 · Trips and emergency shutdown

After a trip: read, secure, hold the heat

1 · Read

First-out on the SIS tab. Confirm XV-103 closed.

2 · Secure

FIC-103 and AIC-104 to MAN, stop the sulfur pump.

3 · Hold heat

Long repair: sweep briefly, stop K-101, then acid pumps.

4 · Restart

Fix the cause, then the hot restart.

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • Watch stack SO₂, bed 1 exit, bed rises and bypass valve room.
  • Sulfur rate makes acid; strength and inlets decide the stack.
  • Optimise inlets one at a time and let pass 2 settle.
  • Heat first, sulfur last; HV-112 locked shut before sulfur.
  • Stop the blower after the sweep: the catalyst stays hot for hours.

1 · The unit in one picture

Block flow of the converter section

Battery limits: dried air in, molten sulfur in, acid and steam out, tail gas to the stack. The air-drying tower and acid product system are not simulated.

2 · Air, sulfur, furnace and boiler

Making the converter feedwalk 1 of 4

K-101 · 238.5 kNm³/h, 60 kPa g→FV-101 · 204.4 to F-101→F-101 · 1121 °C, 14 % SO₂, 7 % O₂→B-101 · 274 °C, 94 t/h steam
TV-201 · hot bypass 35 %+FV-102 · 34.1 dilution air→bed 1 · 420 °C, 12 % SO₂, 9 % O₂

Sulfur (40.9 t/h, steam-traced near 140 °C) reaches the burner through P-101A/B, XV-103 and FV-103.

3 · Pass 1 and the interpass exchangers

Three beds, three coolerswalk 2 of 4

bed 1 · 420 → 631 °C · 63.1 %→SH-201 · → 598→E-201 · → 445 (TV-211)
bed 2 · 445 → 528 °C · 88.1 %→E-202 · → 440 (TV-221)
bed 3 · 440 → 465 °C · 95.8 %→E-203 · → 190 °C (TV-251)→T-301

SH-201 superheats the boiler steam; E-201 and E-202 give their heat to the return gas; E-203 heats boiler feed water.

4 · IPA and the return gas

Absorb, then reheatwalk 3 of 4

T-301 IPA · 1600 m³/h of 98.5 % acid at 80 °C→gas out 83 °C, 0.60 % SO₂, SO₃ ≈ 0
E-202 cold side · 83 → 204 °C→E-201 cold side · 204 → 425 °C→bed 4

Acid absorbs 99.95 % of the SO₃; water added to the circulating acid holds 98.5 %.

TV-231 bypasses SH-201: hotter gas reaches E-201, so bed 4 gets hotter.

4 · Pass 2, FAT and stack

Finish the conversion, absorb, dischargewalk 4 of 4

bed 4 · 425 → 441 °C · 99.70 %→E-204 · → 428 (TV-241)→bed 5 · 428 → 427 °C · 99.80 %
E-205 · → 160 °C→T-302 FAT · 1000 m³/h→stack · 196 kNm³/h

At the stack AIT-306 reads 292 ppm SO₂ and AIT-307 10.5 mg/Nm³ acid mist. Acid production is 125 t/h (100 % basis).

Every unit at design: duty and control

K-101 main air blower

238.5 kNm³/h at 90 °C, discharge 60 kPa g, about 4.2 MW. FV-101 55 %, FV-102 45 %.

F-101 sulfur furnace

Burns 40.94 t/h of sulfur: 105.3 MW released, gas 90 → 1121 °C. H-101 off in operation.

B-101 waste heat boiler

Gas 1121 → 274 °C, 94 t/h steam at 4.0 MPa g, about 45 MW. TV-201 bypass 35 %.

SH-201 superheater

Bed 1 gas 631 → 598 °C, steam to 292 °C, 2.2 MW. TV-231 bypass 39 % sets bed 4 inlet.

E-201 hot interpass exchanger

Hot 598 → 406 °C; return gas 204 → 425 °C; 17.2 MW. TV-211 bypass 32 % sets bed 2 inlet.

E-202 cold interpass exchanger

Hot 528 → 416 °C; return gas 83 → 204 °C; 9.2 MW. TV-221 bypass 35 % sets bed 3 inlet.

E-203 economizer

Gas 465 → 130 °C, 190 °C after bypass; BFW out 243 °C; 27.7 MW. TV-251 bypass 30 %.

T-301 intermediate absorber

Gas 190 → 83 °C; acid 1600 m³/h, 98.5 %, 80 °C; 99.95 % of SO₃ absorbed. P-301A running, P-301B on auto.

E-204 economizer

Gas 441 → 423 °C, 428 °C after bypass; 1.0 MW. TV-241 bypass 44 % sets bed 5 inlet.

E-205 economizer

Gas 427 → 160 °C for the FAT; 20.8 MW; no bypass.

T-302 final absorber

Gas in at 160 °C; acid 1000 m³/h; 99.95 % absorbed. P-302A running, P-302B manual spare.

Only the hot-gas bypasses are adjustable — every temperature on the converter is set by how much gas skips an exchanger.

Part 4 · summary

What Part 4 settled

  • Furnace and boiler make 12 % SO₂ gas at 420 °C from air and sulfur.
  • Pass 1 takes it to 95.8 % while E-201/E-202 bank heat for the return gas.
  • T-301 strips the SO₃; beds 4–5 finish at 99.8 %; T-302 cleans the tail gas.
  • Every converter temperature is set by a hot-gas bypass.

3 · Temperature by hot-gas bypass

A bypass valve sets the bed inlet

The valve only chooses how much gas skips the exchanger.

Bypass at 0 %: all gas cooled — the coldest inlet possible. At 100 %: none cooled.

A loop stuck at either end has lost control.

steam from B-101

4 · Fail-safe positions

Instrument air lost: where every valve goes

Closes (FC)

FV-103 sulfur and XV-103: no fuel.
TV-201: all gas through the boiler.
H-101 fuel.

Opens (FO)

FV-101, FV-102: full air purge.
TV-211 … TV-251: exchangers bypassed.

Result

No sulfur, cold air sweeps the beds. Stop K-101 to save the heat.

Part 5 · summary

What Part 5 settled

  • FIC-103 sets the rate; FFC-101 ratio and the AIC-104 cascade set the air.
  • Six TIC loops set temperatures only through hot-gas bypass valves.
  • On air failure sulfur closes and air opens: fuel-free and purged.
  • Six SIS trips close XV-103; eight permissives guard every start.

Part 7 · The units around the converter

What do the other unit operations do, and how does each one limit the converter?

Part 7 · the plan

Five neighbours of R-201

  1. Sulfur feed and furnacemolten sulfur handling and the flame temperature
  2. Waste heat boiler and superheaterturning burning heat into 4 MPa steam
  3. Gas–gas exchangers and economizersthe ε–NTU view, duties and dew point
  4. Absorption towers and acidwhy 98.5 % acid, and what weak acid does
  5. Blower, pressure drop and stackthe air limit behind every production push

1 · Sulfur feed

Molten sulfur: a narrow temperature window

Keep it liquid

Sulfur freezes near 115 °C; lines are steam-jacketed and held near 140 °C.

Not too hot

Above about 160 °C it polymerises and its viscosity jumps.

Keep it clean

Ash and solids are filtered out before the burner.

1 · Sulfur furnace F-101

How hot does the furnace get?

Part 1: burning is complete and releases 297 kJ per mol. All of it first heats the gas.

$y_F$
SO₂ fraction leaving the furnace (set by the air ratio)
–
$T_{ad}$
adiabatic flame temperature
°C
$$T_{ad} = T_{air} + \frac{y_F\,(-\Delta H_S)}{\bar c_p}$$

Real furnace runs lower: refractory and shell losses. OTS: 1121 °C at 14 %.

Interactive · furnace strength

Air ratio, flame temperature and oxygen

From the previous slide$T_{ad} = T_{air} + y_F(-\Delta H_S)/\bar c_p$
$T_{ad}$ (no loss)
O₂ left

Every extra 1 % SO₂ adds about 80 °C to the flame — strong furnace gas saves air but loads the refractory and the boiler.

2 · Waste heat boiler and superheater

B-101 and SH-201: 94 t/h of 4 MPa steam

B-101 · fire-tube

Gas 1121 → 274 °C on boiling water at 250 °C. About 45 MW.

SH-201

Bed 1 exit gas superheats the steam to 292 °C.

Fouling

TI-107 creeps up; TV-201 closes to hold bed 1; margin shrinks.

3 · Gas–gas exchangers and economizers

What limits an exchanger's duty

$C_{min}$
smaller of the two stream heat-capacity flows, $\dot n\bar c_p$
kW/K
NTU
number of transfer units, $UA/C_{min}$: exchanger "size"
–
$\varepsilon$
effectiveness: actual ÷ largest possible duty
–
$$Q = \varepsilon\,C_{min}\,(T_{h,in}-T_{c,in}),\qquad \varepsilon=f(\text{NTU},\,C_{min}/C_{max})$$

Fouling lowers $U$, so NTU and ε fall: less duty at the same bypass.

3 · Gas–gas exchangers and economizers

What each exchanger does for the converter

Duty · E-201

Cools bed 1 gas for bed 2 (TV-211) and heats the return gas to bed 4.

Duty · E-202

Cools bed 2 gas for bed 3 (TV-221) and warms the return gas first.

Dew point · E-203

Gas to the IPA held at 190 °C: acid must not condense on steel.

4 · Absorption towers T-301 and T-302

Why SO₃ goes into 98.5 % acid, not water

Water fails

SO₃ meets water vapour and forms mist that passes the tower.

98.3–98.5 % acid

Lowest SO₃ and water vapour pressure: best absorption.

Strength control

Dilution water holds the circulating acid at 98.5 %.

5 · Blower and pressure drop

60 kPa to push the gas through

About 25 kPa is lost before bed 1 (PI-200 35 kPa g); the beds take about 16 kPa.

Every extra kPa of resistance costs air at the same blower load.

Interactive · the OTS blower and system model

How much air can K-101 deliver?

max air (valves open)
max sulfur at 12 %

Extra bed resistance or a hot afternoon removes production capacity — the air valves saturate before anything in the converter does.

5 · Stack and analyzers

What the stack tells you

AIT-306 · SO₂

292 ppm at design; permit 500; trip 3000 for 5 min.

AIT-307 · mist

10.5 mg/Nm³; alarm 40. Rises with weak or hot acid.

XI-308 · conversion

Calculated from inlet SO₂, air flow and stack SO₂: 99.80 %.

Part 7 · summary

What Part 7 settled

  • Sulfur must stay liquid, clean and near 140 °C; the furnace burns it completely.
  • B-101 and SH-201 recover the burning heat as 4 MPa steam.
  • Exchanger duties and the acid dew point shape what the converter can do.
  • 98.5 % acid absorbs SO₃ best; weak acid raises SO₂ and mist.
  • The blower and the bed resistance set the real production limit.

3 · Troubleshooting · interactive method

The six-stage method, one stage at a time

Training exercises show the fault. Cases hide it, so you need a method, not a memory.

Engage: accept the problem and stay calm

It is your shift's problem now. Tell the supervisor, keep the unit inside its alarm limits, and only then start to think.

Define: what is, and what is not, affected

List the readings that moved and the ones that did not. Write the target: which value must return to which limit.

Explore: check the balances

Compare air, sulfur, heat and pressure with design at the same rate. A reading that breaks a balance is a clue; one that fits them is probably true.

Plan: hypotheses and the test that kills each

Write two or three causes. For each, name one field check or trend that would prove it wrong.

Do it: act safely, predict, compare

Make one change at a time. Say what you expect to see before you move, then compare the trend with your prediction.

Look back: make it not happen again

Record the cause, the evidence and the fix. Propose the alarm, check or procedure change that would catch it earlier.

Plan is where most cases are won — never let one instrument be both the symptom and its own proof.

3 · Troubleshooting cases · Engage, Define, Explore, Plan, Do it, Look back

TE-1 and TE-21 of 6

TE-1Stack SO2 creeping up

ObjectiveSeparate an equipment problem from an operating-point problem with balances and field checks.

SituationOver the last hour the stack SO2 analyzer has crept from about 290 to about 440 ppm. Sulfur rate, strength and every bed inlet temperature are at their set points. The previous shift saw nothing unusual.

TE-2The air valves keep opening

ObjectiveFind where a slowly growing limit comes from before it takes the margin.

SituationConverter at design rate. Over the week FV-101 and FV-102 have been opening further and the converter inlet pressure PI-200 is about 10 kPa above what it was after the turnaround.

4 · Prediction drills

What-if: predict before the model runs

ObjectivePredict the direction each variable moves 30 minutes after a change, then check against a copy of the model.

Variables: FI-100 total air, TI-203 bed 1 exit, TI-213 bed 2 exit, TI-233 bed 4 exit, AI-105 O2 into bed 1, AIT-306 stack SO2, AIT-307 stack SO3 mist, FI-309 acid production.

The six events

  • Sulfur +10 % (FIC-103 SP 45 t/h)
  • SO2 strength +1 % (AIC-104 SP 13 %)
  • Bed 1 inlet +10 °C (TIC-201 SP 430)
  • Bed 3 inlet −10 °C (TIC-221 SP 430)
  • Bed 4 inlet +10 °C (TIC-231 SP 435)
  • one equipment upset, named when you run it

Part 8 · summary

What Part 8 settled

  • Read the objective first; it tells you what the exercise is really testing.
  • Training exercises show one clean disturbance; cases hide the cause.
  • Use the six stages: engage, define, explore, plan, do it, look back.
  • Procedures are graded on order and safety; the score punishes the stack, heat and ignored alarms.

Closing

Key Takeaways

1

Keep each bed above its strike temperature and bed 1 below 640 °C.

2

Read conversion from the bed rises: 3.35 °C per % at 12 % SO₂.

3

Protect the IPA: removing SO₃ is what turns 96 % into 99.8 %.

4

Verify an instrument in the field before trusting the loop it drives.

5

After a stop, sweep briefly, then stop the blower to keep the heat.
